title: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras
body_text:
Under Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), a total of 20,149 Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) have been opened across the country till 30.06.2026, out of which 1833 JAKs have been opened in the State of Kerala. The district-wise number of JAKs opened in the State of Kerala is at Annexure.
The product basket under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojna has 2,110 medicines and 315 surgicals, medical consumables and devices, covering all major therapeutic groups, such as cardiovascular, anti-cancer, anti-diabetic, anti-infectives, anti-allergic and gastro-intestinal medicines and nutraceuticals.
During the last five financial years i.e. 2021-22 to 2025-26, PMBJP has made sales of Rs. 7,873.85 crore through Jan Aushadhi Kendras across the country which has led to savings of approximately Rs. 37,200 crore to the citizens.
Government has adopted a franchise-like model for opening of Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs). Any individual entrepreneurs, non-governmental organisations, societies, trusts, firms, private companies, etc., can apply for opening of Jan Aushadhi Kendras, through the scheme’s website ( www.janaushadhi.gov.in ) across the country including those in Kerala. To facilitate the opening of Jan Aushadhi Kendras in the underserved areas, Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI) is regularly writing letters to the concerned administration/district magistrate for providing free space to the applicants in government hospitals.
To address supply gaps and ensure uninterrupted availability of products at JAKs, the following measures have been put in place:
Since September 2024, stocking by JAKs of 200 commonly used medicines, consisting of the 100 top-selling medicines in the scheme product basket and 100 fast-selling medicines in the market, has been incentivised, under which JAK owners are eligible for monthly incentive based on the stocks that they maintain for these medicines. An end-to-end information-technology-enabled supply chain system connects a robust supply chain system comprising five warehouses and a growing network of distributors across the country, currently numbering 42. In addition, with a view to ensure availability of commonly used products, 400 fast-moving products are monitored regularly by Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), the scheme implementing agency, and demand for the same is estimated on a continuous basis. Further, steps have been taken to digitise the estimation method to augment the procurement process.
To ensure that only quality medicines are supplied through Jan Aushadhi Kendras, the following quality assurance mechanisms have been put in place:
(i) Procurement only from WHO-GMP certified manufacturers: Medicines are procured only from pharmaceutical units compliant with World Health Organization-Good Manufacturing Practices (WHO-GMP).
(ii) Distribution only after 100% pre-testing of all medicine batches: Random testing of 100% batches supplied at PMBI’s warehouses, and medicines are dispatched for supply to JAKs only after successful quality test.
(iii) Testing through NABL-accredited laboratories : Samples are tested only in laboratories accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), which are also assessed by PMBI for compliance with Good Laboratory Practices (GLP).

This information was given by Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Smt. Anupriya Patel, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

enrichment.summary: As of 30 June 2026, 20,149 Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) have been opened across India under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), including 1,833 in Kerala. The scheme's product basket includes 2,110 medicines and 315 surgicals/consumables, and over FY2021-22 to FY2025-26 it generated sales of Rs. 7,873.85 crore, saving citizens an estimated Rs. 37,200 crore. The Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers detailed the franchise model for opening JAKs, supply-chain measures, and quality assurance mechanisms in a Rajya Sabha written reply.
enrichment.context:
PMBJP, launched in 2008 and administered by the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI) under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, aims to provide quality generic medicines at affordable prices through dedicated outlets, reducing out-of-pocket health expenditure—a key concern given India's high share of private, out-of-pocket healthcare spending. The scheme is central to the government's affordable healthcare agenda alongside Ayushman Bharat and price-control mechanisms under the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), and it supports the broader goal of Universal Health Coverage by making essential medicines accessible even in remote and underserved districts.

The franchise-like model, open to individuals, NGOs, trusts, and private entities, has enabled rapid scaling of outlets, while the government's push to provide free space in government hospitals targets equity in underserved regions. Quality assurance—procurement only from WHO-GMP certified manufacturers, 100% batch pre-testing, and NABL-accredited lab testing—addresses past criticisms about drug quality in low-cost generic programs. The 2024 incentive scheme for stocking 200 commonly used medicines and the expanding warehouse-distributor network reflect efforts to fix supply-chain bottlenecks, a recurring challenge in scheme implementation, and align with India's push to digitise procurement and inventory management across public health systems.

prelims_questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) is implemented by which of the following agencies?
options: Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI)
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly identifies the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI) as the scheme implementing agency responsible for monitoring products and ensuring supply and quality under PMBJP.

prelims_questions.question: With reference to quality assurance under PMBJP, consider the following statements: 1. Medicines are procured only from WHO-GMP certified manufacturers. 2. Testing of medicine batches is done only in NABL-accredited laboratories. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that medicines are procured only from WHO-GMP compliant units and that samples are tested only in NABL-accredited laboratories, confirming both statements as correct.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana in reducing out-of-pocket health expenditure in India. What supply-chain and quality-assurance challenges does the scheme face, and how are they being addressed?
